Comment: PB-1 'Bundle Enrollment' — Setup steps 1-6. AUTHORED SPEC ARTIFACT: this state machine documents the intended orchestration shape (ADR-002: workflow orchestrates, domain owns rules — no business logic lives here, only sequencing/error routing). It is registered on LocalStack (best-effort, see scripts/provision.ts) for parse-validation purposes only. It is NOT the executed engine for this pilot: the automatic Task states below target arn:aws:states:::apigateway:invoke, the one HTTP-style connector that LocalStack Community's ASL parser recognizes, but no API Gateway REST API is actually deployed anywhere in this repo (every BC is an in-process Hono app, invoked directly in tests/orchestrator code, never fronted by API Gateway or Lambda). Real execution of steps 1-6 is instead driven by workflow/pb-1-orchestrator.ts (the L2 fallback), which calls the same BC entrypoints in-process and polls DynamoDB read models in place of Activity task-token callbacks. See that file's header comment for the decision-4 rationale.

CreateEvent.Comment: Steps 1-2 combined: O3 POST /events creates the sport event AND its categorie in one call (O3's handler accepts categorie in the request body, publishing EventPublished). Resource is arn:aws:states:::apigateway:invoke — the only http-shaped connector LocalStack Community's parser accepts; arn:aws:states:::http:invoke is rejected at CreateStateMachine time ('Unknown service: http'). ApiEndpoint/ApiId/Stage are placeholders: in production these would resolve from CDK-exported API Gateway stage outputs for the O3 BC; here no API Gateway is deployed, so this Task can only ever be parsed, never actually invoked end-to-end.

OpenRegistrationWindow.Comment: Step 3: O5 POST /events/{sportEventId}/registration-window:open. sportEventId threads forward from CreateEvent's ResultPath (createEventResult.sportEventId). Same apigateway:invoke placeholder caveat as CreateEvent — O5 is also an in-process Hono app with no API Gateway front door in this pilot.

WaitForApplication.Comment: Step 4: pause the execution until a participant actually applies (RegistrationApplied domain event), i.e. a genuine .waitForTaskToken-style callback. Resource is an Activity ARN placeholder substituted at provision time (see scripts/provision.ts, which creates the 'pb-1-registration-applied-activity' Activity and string-replaces this token before CreateStateMachine). A worker would call GetActivityTask against this ARN, block until O5's RegistrationApplied handler (or an EventBridge rule targeting the activity via a small poller) calls SendTaskSuccess with the registrationId. This Activity/GetActivityTask/SendTaskSuccess round trip was empirically verified to work on LocalStack Community; the blocker for this pilot is exclusively the preceding Task states' lack of an invocable REST target, not this callback mechanism.

ConfirmTeam.Comment: Step 5: O5 POST /registrations/{registrationId}/confirm. This is the human-in-the-loop step referenced in the brief: confirmation requires a RegistrationManager-authorized caller (see HttpClaimAuthorizer), so in practice a human/organizer action surfaces this as a manual approval — a read-model/dashboard view can observe the registration sitting in 'Applied' status awaiting this Task to fire. Same apigateway:invoke placeholder caveat as the earlier Task states.

WaitForFeePaid.Comment: Step 6: pause again until ParticipationFeePaid is observed (O12 pay -> O5's onFeePaid auto-confirm). Same Activity-ARN placeholder / task-token pattern as WaitForApplication, substituted at provision time with the 'pb-1-fee-paid-activity' Activity ARN.

SetupComplete.Comment: PB-1 Setup steps 1-6 complete: event created, registration window open, a participant applied, was confirmed by a RegistrationManager, and paid the participation fee.

HumanReview.Comment: Structural error-routing target only (ADR-002: workflow orchestrates, domain owns rules — no business-rule logic here). When a domain Task rejects with a 409/422 (e.g. DoubleApplyError, WindowClosedError, NotAuthorizedError), the execution lands here instead of failing outright, representing a queue/dashboard row for manual operator intervention. A real deployment would route this to an SNS topic, a support queue, or a read-model flag; this pilot models only the state-machine shape, not that integration.
